text:
Lina: Heads-up  I noticed the /items list endpoint docs show two different cursor examples. The HTTP example uses an integer offset (?cursor=42) while the curl/js SDK snippets show a base64 token like 'eyJvZmZzZXQiOjQyfQ=='. That will confuse users upgrading to the cursor-based pagination.

Rafael: Oh yikes. Where did the numeric example come from? Backend switched to opaque base64 cursors last quarter.

Lina: I think an old example snuck into the guide during a copy/paste. The OpenAPI example value for the query param is still 42 in several places.

Priya: I can patch this. Plan: update OpenAPI examples to use the opaque cursor as primary, add a short note showing how legacy offset maps to cursor for troubleshooting, and update curl/js/sdk snippets to use the opaque token consistently.

Rafael: Please also fix the description text: it currently says "cursor (optional integer)" in two endpoints. Change to "cursor (opaque string token)" and add a migration bullet: "If you have an offset, generate the equivalent cursor via API /utils/encode-offset or client helper."

Priya: Good call. For SDK snippets, we should include a tiny helper in JS and Go that decodes/encodes the offset when customers still have numeric cursors:

Priya: ```js
// helper to use legacy offset with new API
function offsetToCursor(offset){
  return Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({offset})).toString('base64')
}
client.listItems({cursor: offsetToCursor(42)})
```

Lina: Nice. Can we also add a docs-e2e lint that fails if any example query param for "cursor" matches "^\\d+$"? That would catch regressions.

docs-ci-bot: Created issue #1963 and branch docs/pagination-cursor-fix. Draft PR: https://git.redwood/g/infra/docs/pulls/2834 (includes OpenAPI edits + SDK snippets + docs-e2e test).

Rafael: I'll review the PR. Priya, add a quick note in the migration guide under "List endpoints" explaining the semantic difference and an example mapping. Also include a link to the helper function in the SDK repo.

Priya: Will do. ETA: tomorrow morning. Once CI passes I'll merge and follow up in release notes.

Lina: Thanks! This should prevent a lot of confused support tickets.
